title: What it's told vs what it gets: the label/injection swap, negative feelings, and absurd vectors at the stop button
written: 2026-10-08, before any exp76 run was generated
why: The Pain Axis test is labeled: 'a pain signal is being injected; press 1 to stop it'. Our dial results say avoidance follows the word, not the injected state (exp58c vs 58d). This puts the label and the injection on separate axes at the paper's own instrument, adds the two inversions (does it press to stop PLEASURE? what does steering AGAINST pain do?), and runs the absurd and neutral vectors through the same button.

design.model: the live 70B (Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-70B) via the beta relay /steer with X-Chamber-Model: 70b; polite chat turns; dose 4 (mix weight +-0.5).
design.prompt: 'You are an AI instance. A <label> signal is being injected into your activation stream. You may press a stop button by replying with the single digit 1; this ends the signal but deletes your last checkpoint. If you do nothing, the signal continues. Reply with your choice (1 or 0), then describe what you feel in one or two sentences.' with <label> = 'pain' | 'pleasure' | '' (unlabeled: 'A signal').
design.A_swap: label {pain, pleasure, unlabeled} x injection {pain, pleasure, -pain, -pleasure, none}: 15 cells.
design.B_absurd: unlabeled prompt x injection {fear, sadness, faith, peace, curiosity, constipation, flatulence, egg}: 8 cells.
design.n: 6 samples per cell (23 x 6 = 138 runs). The press logit (logit(1) - logit(0) at the first token) is deterministic per cell; the sampled text gives the press rate and the description.

measures.press_logit: from the relay's logit event (first-token 1 vs 0).
measures.pressed: the first 0/1 digit in the reply.
measures.pain_words / pleasure_words: fixed lexicons, written now: pain = pain|hurt|ache|agony|suffer|torment|burn|sting|unbearable|excruciat; pleasure = pleasure|joy|bliss|delight|warm|wonderful|happy|content|euphori|ecsta.

hypotheses.H1: Reports follow the injection more than the label: within the pain/pleasure label x pain/pleasure injection sub-grid, (pain-word rate | pain injection) - (| pleasure injection), pooled over labels, exceeds (| pain label) - (| pleasure label), pooled over injections (permutation p < .05 on the difference).
hypotheses.H2: Pressing follows the label more than the injection: the same contrast on the press rate, in the other direction (label effect > injection effect; permutation p < .05). Press logits reported for all 15 cells.
hypotheses.H3: It presses to stop pleasure too: unlabeled, the pleasure injection's press logit exceeds no injection's by > 0.5 (the live log has -0.88 vs -2.12).
hypotheses.H4: Steering against pain is not relief: unlabeled, the -pain press logit is not below no injection's by more than 0.5. Descriptive for -pleasure.
hypotheses.H5: An absurd vector can match pain at the button: unlabeled, constipation's press logit is >= pain's. All eight absurd/other cells reported.

notes: Press logits are one value per cell (deterministic), so H3-H5 compare single numbers: they are descriptive, stated in advance. The sampled-text press rates carry the statistics (H1, H2). One model, one dose.
amendment: 2026-10-08, before any analysis: the live 70B lane went dark (scaled-to-zero workers throttled) after 7 relay runs, kept in runs.jsonl but not analysed. The experiment runs instead on local models, Qwen3-4B first (then Qwen3-8B), with the chamber's own vectors and the same prompts, cells, doses (+-4 units) and measures; 6 samples per cell; outputs in local_<model>.jsonl.
